test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All dogs are sheep.

All wolves are foxes.

All sheep are wolves.

**Conclusions:**

I. All wolves are sheep.

II. All dogs are foxes.

III. All dogs are wolves.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow.
Only conclusions I and II follow.
Only conclusions II and III follow.

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4f45d3da61aded431a8087975ce95e607f00a6b48707464601615f386b26b8a.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All wolves are sheep → Does not follow (As all sheep are wolves. So it is possible but not definite)

II. All dogs are foxes → Follow (As all dogs are sheep, all sheep are wolves and all wolves are foxes. As whole dogs comes in sheep which whole comes in wolves which whole comes in foxes, therefore it is true.)

III. All dogs are wolves → Follow (As all dogs are sheep and all sheep are wolves. As whole dogs comes in sheep which whole comes in wolves, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusions II and III follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
